text:
maria: quick thread — thinking about TLS handling for private endpoints. proposal: use SNI passthrough at the regional NLB and terminate TLS in the tenant VPC sidecar (customer-managed certs) instead of terminating at our control plane. fewer cert obligations for us and preserves end-to-end auth.
aj: curious about observability tradeoffs. if we do passthrough we lose HTTP-level metrics at CP. can we get enough telemetry from sidecars?
sam: we could add a small trace/span relay from sidecars -> CP observability pipeline. basically emit a lightweight span with request_id, latency, outcome. no headers leaked.
maria: exactly. sidecars already have our agent identity so they can sign the span. avoids us storing tenant certs and mitigates compliance risk.
taylor: ok but what about routing fallback? currently CP needs to inspect host header to pick the right tenant backend. with passthrough we need SNI->route table mapping in the relay layer. is that manageable?
aj: SNI mapping is stable — tenants register CN/SAN when they onboard. mapping lives in a control config pushed to regional relays. relay uses a fast in-memory map; lookups are O(1).
sam: one operational quirk: some client libs don't set SNI for IP-based calls or if they use HTTP/1.0. we should fallback to an explicit endpoint hostname mechanism (tenant-specific endpoint hostname) documented for SDKs.
maria: agreed — doc + SDK validation. fallback mode: if SNI absent, relay checks ALPN and last-resort routing header we add via binaries in private networks.
taylor: another concern: mTLS between customer and sidecar vs our mTLS between sidecar and control plane. If sidecar terminates TLS, customer auth is preserved locally; we then use mutual TLS to CP with a short-lived cert. sounds ok.
aj: cost-wise, keeping TLS passthrough at regional ingress means using NLB (L4) not ALB (L7) — cheaper and scales better for high-conn-count. win.
sam: but we lose the ability to do protocol-aware WAF rules at CP. do we want any centralized WAF?
maria: for regulated tenants we can offer an optional CP-termination SKU: we host TLS, run inspection, and provide additional policy hooks. default stays passthrough.
taylor: migration plan? we have thousands of tenants on existing CP-terminated endpoints.
aj: plan: 1) new tenants default to passthrough + sidecar cert flow. 2) staged migration for existing tenants with opt-in tooling and a compatibility window of 90 days. 3) offer CP-termination if customer requests.
sam: need an experiment to validate perf and error modes: create a canary region, route 5% traffic for migrated tenants over passthrough and compare latency, error surface, observability completeness.
maria: action items: @aj create infra perf spike and cost estimate; @sam prototype the span relay + schema; @taylor draft SDK fallback and onboarding flow; I'll author an RFC with diagrams and rollout timeline.
infra-bot: deploy:canary started for region-us-west-2 (job id: deploy-2026-03-sni-canary). :white_check_mark:
aj: will also add a health-check probe: TCP handoff + TLS handshake time metric to detect clients without SNI.
taylor: one more thought — cert rotation: sidecars will pull ephemeral certs from their tenant KMS or our issuance gateway. need to ensure short TTLs and automated retry.
maria: yep. include failure modes in RFC: 1) missing SNI -> instruct SDK to use explicit hostname 2) sidecar cert fetch failure -> fallback to CP-termination for that tenant 3) relay mapping inconsistency -> route to degraded mode and emit alerts.
sam: sounds good. I'll capture the telemetry spec (span fields + sampling).
aj: I'll post cost delta (NLB vs ALB + added sidecar CPU) by Friday.
maria: thanks all. RFC target EOW.
